newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force chief may be promoted despite affair.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force chief may be promoted despite affair.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen on Thursdayy decided to retain Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston as a leading candidate to become the top U.S. military commander despite Ralston's adulterous affair 14 years ago.

"We need to come back to a rule of reason instead of a rule of thumb," Cohen told the Washington Post in an interview published on Thursday, after discussing the matter with President Bill Clinton and Ralston.

Ralston, currently vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and Cohen's favourite to become chairman, had not told Pentagon officials about the affair he had with a CIA employee until news organisations inquired about the matter this week, the Post said.
Cohen told the paper the affair was about a year long and occurred while Ralston and his wife, Linda, were separated. The Ralstons reconciled for a time, but divorced in 1988.
Ralston, travelling in Kazakstan, denied through a senior Cohen aide that his affair continued during the time he reconciled with Linda, the Post said. He has since remarried.

Adultery is a crime in the military. Although the Pentagon rarely prosecutes soldiers and officers for adultery, service members have often been forced into early retirement or had their pay and rank reduced.

Cohen told the Post he would wait another week or two before making a final recommendation to Clinton, possibly to gauge public opinion. Retiring Joint Staffs Chief John Shalikashvili also backed Ralston.

News of Ralston's adulterous affair came just after Air Force Major Kelly Flinn, the first female B-52 pilot, agreed to accept a general discharge rather than face a court-martial for an adulterous affair.
Cohen on Tuesday said there was no epidemic of sex harassment or marital cheating in the U.S. military and praised the armed forces for dealing openly with recent embarrassing cases.

The commanding general of the Army's scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground base in Maryland, Maj. Gen. John Longhouser, announced on Tuesday that he was retiring and admitted he had had an adulterous affair five years ago.
